title: Assessment of intrinsic bioremediation of jet fuel contamination in a shallow aquifer, Beaufort, South Carolina
citation: Chapelle, F.H., Landmeyer, J.E., and Bradley, P.M., 1996, Assessment of intrinsic bioremediation of jet fuel contamination in a shallow aquifer, Beaufort, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Water-Resources Investigations Report 95-4262, map scale 1:1,940.
notes:
Contaminant-hydrology report. The two core logs (fig. 2, p. 10) are graphic: layer boundaries are drawn against a depth scale and cannot be read as numbers from the text, so intervals carry descriptions only, in log order, with no top/bottom. Water-chemistry tables 1-4 and model parameters were not recorded (not geologic). Monitoring-well water levels on the fig. 1 map were not legible in the text layer. Page 14 says ground water flows 'from east to west toward low-lying areas east of the site' as printed; quoted as is. All six references recorded.
Re-read of pages 15-18 for water tests: Tables 1-4 (BTEX and naphthalene; field-measured DO, ferrous iron, sulfide, pH, dissolved hydrogen and temperature; anions and gases; cations), one entry per well and parameter, all sampled March 9, 1994. NA (not analyzed) cells skipped. Less-than values kept as printed (e.g. <5.0, <.05). Column headers of Table 3 and Table 2 checked on page images; Table 3 labels printed with a space in the text layer (BFT-TF-1 1) and methane <-1 (read <.1) flagged inferred. Replicate rows: BFT-401-3 (replicate), BFT-RW (replicate), BFT-RWR (replicate) and BFT-TF-RW (replicate) linked to wells BFT-401-3 and BFT-RW (the last two inferred). Range statements in the text (hydrogen 0.1 to 1.5 nM, sulfate 0.8 to 150 mg/L, phosphate below 0.01 mg/L) not recorded as tests.
